topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning aims regarding cancer treatment approaches and their modes of action.

topics.label: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutics, detailing their mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance via efflux pumps.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cellular Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively target cancer cell vulnerabilities, such as hormone dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, oncolytic viral sensitivity, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeting Oncogenic Kinases and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale of oncogene addiction, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting ATP-binding pockets, and the subsequent emergence of resistance mutations, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe antibody-based interventions used to block receptor signaling, recruit immune effector mechanisms, or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Immune Surveillance and Immune Checkpoint Blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for anti-tumor immune responses and examine the therapeutic reactivation of exhausted T cells using checkpoint inhibitors against tumor neoantigens.

topics.label: Cellular and Bispecific Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss engineered immunological strategies designed to redirect or enhance T-cell cytotoxicity against cancer cells, specifically bispecific T-cell engagers and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesise the broader landscape of cancer treatment by considering tumor heterogeneity, historical survival trends, early detection, and the future clinical and ethical dilemmas of patient management.
